label: Matt 10:1
text: He called to himself his twelve disciples, and gave them authority over unclean spirits, to cast them out, and to heal every disease and every sickness.

label: Matt 10:2
text: Now the names of the twelve apostles are these. The first, Simon, who is called Peter; Andrew, his brother; James the son of Zebedee; John, his brother;

label: Matt 10:3
text: Philip; Bartholomew; Thomas; Matthew the tax collector; James the son of Alphaeus; Lebbaeus, who was also called Thaddaeus;

variants.note: The fetched Wikipedia 'Textual variants in the Gospel of Matthew' lists Θαδδαιος (Thaddaeus) in א (Sinaiticus) and B (Vaticanus), with later minuscules and versions - the name without Lebbaeus.

The article lists Λεββαιος (Lebbaeus) in D (Codex Bezae) and Origen's Latin text; neither is a manuscript node of this graph, so attested_by is left empty. The WEB text of this passage, 'Lebbaeus, who was also called Thaddaeus', is the majority (Byzantine) reading, which the article shows in C2, E-K, N, W, Δ, Θ, Π, Σ, f1 and Byz - Codex Washingtonianus (W) among them.

label: Matt 10:4
text: Simon the Canaanite; and Judas Iscariot, who also betrayed him.

label: Matt 10:5
text:
Jesus sent these twelve out, and commanded them, saying,
“Don’t go among the Gentiles, and don’t enter into any city of the Samaritans.

label: Matt 10:6
text: Rather, go to the lost sheep of the house of Israel.

label: Matt 10:7
text: As you go, preach, saying, ‘The Kingdom of Heaven is at hand!’

label: Matt 10:8
text:
Heal the sick, cleanse the lepers,
and cast out demons. Freely you received, so freely give.

label: Matt 10:9
text: Don’t take any gold, silver, or brass in your money belts.

label: Matt 10:10
text: Take no bag for your journey, neither two coats, nor shoes, nor staff: for the laborer is worthy of his food.

label: Matt 10:11
text: Into whatever city or village you enter, find out who in it is worthy; and stay there until you go on.

label: Matt 10:12
text: As you enter into the household, greet it.

label: Matt 10:13
text: If the household is worthy, let your peace come on it, but if it isn’t worthy, let your peace return to you.

label: Matt 10:14
text: Whoever doesn’t receive you, nor hear your words, as you go out of that house or that city, shake the dust off your feet.

label: Matt 10:15
text: Most certainly I tell you, it will be more tolerable for the land of Sodom and Gomorrah in the day of judgment than for that city.

label: Matt 10:16
text: “Behold, I send you out as sheep among wolves. Therefore be wise as serpents, and harmless as doves.

label: Matt 10:17
text: But beware of men: for they will deliver you up to councils, and in their synagogues they will scourge you.

label: Matt 10:18
text: Yes, and you will be brought before governors and kings for my sake, for a testimony to them and to the nations.

label: Matt 10:19
text: But when they deliver you up, don’t be anxious how or what you will say, for it will be given you in that hour what you will say.

label: Matt 10:20
text: For it is not you who speak, but the Spirit of your Father who speaks in you.

label: Matt 10:21
text: “Brother will deliver up brother to death, and the father his child. Children will rise up against parents, and cause them to be put to death.

label: Matt 10:22
text: You will be hated by all men for my name’s sake, but he who endures to the end will be saved.

label: Matt 10:23
text: But when they persecute you in this city, flee into the next, for most certainly I tell you, you will not have gone through the cities of Israel, until the Son of Man has come.

label: Matt 10:24
text: “A disciple is not above his teacher, nor a servant above his lord.

label: Matt 10:25
text:
It is enough for the disciple that he be like his teacher, and the servant like his lord. If they have called the master of the house Beelzebul,
how much more those of his household!

label: Matt 10:26
text: Therefore don’t be afraid of them, for there is nothing covered that will not be revealed; and hidden that will not be known.

label: Matt 10:27
text: What I tell you in the darkness, speak in the light; and what you hear whispered in the ear, proclaim on the housetops.

label: Matt 10:28
text: Don’t be afraid of those who kill the body, but are not able to kill the soul. Rather, fear him who is able to destroy both soul and body in Gehenna.

label: Matt 10:29
text:
“Aren’t two sparrows sold for an assarion coin?
Not one of them falls on the ground apart from your Father’s will,

label: Matt 10:30
text: but the very hairs of your head are all numbered.

label: Matt 10:31
text: Therefore don’t be afraid. You are of more value than many sparrows.

label: Matt 10:32
text: Everyone therefore who confesses me before men, him I will also confess before my Father who is in heaven.

label: Matt 10:33
text: But whoever denies me before men, him I will also deny before my Father who is in heaven.

label: Matt 10:34
text: “Don’t think that I came to send peace on the earth. I didn’t come to send peace, but a sword.

label: Matt 10:35
text: For I came to set a man at odds against his father, and a daughter against her mother, and a daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law.

label: Matt 10:36
text: A man’s foes will be those of his own household.

label: Matt 10:37
text: He who loves father or mother more than me is not worthy of me; and he who loves son or daughter more than me isn’t worthy of me.

label: Matt 10:38
text: He who doesn’t take his cross and follow after me, isn’t worthy of me.

label: Matt 10:39
text: He who seeks his life will lose it; and he who loses his life for my sake will find it.

label: Matt 10:40
text: He who receives you receives me, and he who receives me receives him who sent me.

label: Matt 10:41
text: He who receives a prophet in the name of a prophet will receive a prophet’s reward. He who receives a righteous man in the name of a righteous man will receive a righteous man’s reward.

label: Matt 10:42
text: Whoever gives one of these little ones just a cup of cold water to drink in the name of a disciple, most certainly I tell you he will in no way lose his reward.”

statement: Jesus chose twelve disciples, gave them authority over unclean spirits and disease, and sent them out.
label: The Twelve sent out with authority

statement: The Twelve are named: Simon Peter, Andrew, James and John the sons of Zebedee, Philip, Bartholomew, Thomas, Matthew the tax collector, James son of Alphaeus, Thaddaeus, Simon the Zealot (Cananaean) and Judas Iscariot.
label: The names of the Twelve

statement: Matthew, one of the Twelve, was a tax collector.
label: Matthew the tax collector

statement: Judas bears the epithet 'Iscariot', whose meaning is disputed (man of Kerioth; a form of sicarius, 'dagger man'; 'the liar').
label: The epithet 'Iscariot'

statement: Simon is called 'the Zealot' (Cananaean), matching the Zealot movement ('fourth philosophy') of first-century Judea.
label: Simon the Zealot and the Zealot movement

statement: The mission is restricted to Israel: the Twelve are told not to go among the Gentiles or into Samaritan cities.
label: Mission limited to Israel

statement: The Samaritans were a distinct people of the land, centred on Shechem and Mount Gerizim, with their own temple.
label: The Samaritans and their Gerizim temple

statement: Gold, silver and bronze/copper coinage circulated in Judea and was carried on the person (in the belt).
label: Coinage in the money belt

statement: Travelers carried a bag, tunics, sandals and a staff: the standard travel gear of the period.
label: Travel gear (bag, tunics, sandals, staff)

statement: Shaking the dust off one's feet when leaving a rejecting house or city, a gesture of testimony against it.
label: Shaking off the dust

statement: Sodom and Gomorrah were destroyed and remembered in the first century as objects of divine judgment.
label: Sodom and Gomorrah

statement: Wolves lived in the region and preyed on sheep, so sending disciples out 'as sheep among wolves' was a real image.
label: Sheep among wolves

statement: Venomous snakes were familiar dangers in the region ('wise as serpents').
label: Serpents of the region

statement: Disciples would be delivered up to councils (synedria) and flogged: councils and synagogues acted as judicial institutions, and flogging was a court punishment.
label: Councils, synagogues and flogging

statement: Believers would be brought before governors and kings: Roman governors ruled provinces such as Judaea.
label: Governors and kings

statement: 'Beelzebul' was a current name for the ruler of demons; its etymology is disputed.
label: Beelzebul

statement: Two sparrows were sold for one assarion, a small bronze/copper coin of the lowest value.
label: Two sparrows for an assarion

statement: The sword (machaira) was a familiar weapon in Judea.
label: The sword

statement: Crucifixion was a Roman punishment used in Judaea before 30 CE, so 'take up his cross' pointed to a known death.
label: Crucifixion in Judaea

statement: Giving a cup of cold water to drink was an act of hospitality toward those on the road.
label: A cup of cold water
